name: Bump Steer Correction
description: Bump steer is toe change with suspension travel caused by the tie rod not following the arc of the lower links/strut. Lowering a Gen 6 Camaro or changing radius rods/LCAs changes it; it is corrected by moving the outer tie rod pivot height with an adjustable tie rod end and spacers, measured with a bump-steer gauge.

components.name: Bump-steer adjustable outer tie rod ends
components.description: Replace the OE outer tie rod ends with a chromoly shank, spherical rod end and spacer stack so the outer pivot height can be moved to match the lower-link geometry. Also prevents inner tie rod binding on heavily lowered cars.
components.location: Knuckle steering arm, approx (x -0.12, y 0.25, z +/-0.68).

raceOptions.name: SPL Parts TRE CAM6 bumpsteer adjustable front tie rod ends
raceOptions.notes: 4140 chromoly shanks, 2024 aluminum turnbuckles, Teflon-lined FK rod ends (19 deg misalignment), stainless spacers. Designed for 19-20 in wheels; 18 in wheels require cutting the stud.

hardware.item: Rod end bolt through steering arm
hardware.torque: Per SPL instructions (not in available source)

installNotes: Set total length equal to OE tie rod end center-to-center first, then fine-tune toe.
Check wheel barrel clearance at full lock and full bump.
inspection: Check rod-end play and turnbuckle lock each event.

images.title: SPL Parts FLCA CAM6 front lower control arm (Gen 6 Camaro)

modelRef.features: Rod end on a vertical stud with spacer stack for bump-steer height, threaded shank inboard

components.name: Bump steer spacer stack
components.description: Stainless steel spacers of several thicknesses that move the rod end up/down on the shank to change outer tie rod height. Typical aim: less than approx 0.010 in (0.25 mm) toe change per inch of travel through +/-2 in of travel, with slight toe-out in bump preferred by many racers.
components.location: On tie rod end shank at steering arm.

specs.Target: < approx 0.010 in toe change per in of travel (typical)

installNotes: Measure with springs removed (or with a bump-steer fixture), moving the hub through travel in 1/2 in steps.

components.name: Bump steer gauge / measurement fixture (tool)
components.description: Plate bolted to the hub with dial indicators (or a laser) that measure toe change as the suspension is cycled with the spring removed or a solid spacer in place of the damper. Used with the adjustable tie rod ends to set bump steer after ride height and alignment geometry are final.
components.location: Bolted to front hub (tool, not installed on car).
installNotes: Lock steering at center; support chassis at race ride height on stands.
